# Feedback receiver (Деталь 3.8, F-2)

Write-only приёмник баг-репортов: `POST /report` → GitHub Issue в
`DeadSno/agent-steward`. Никаких данных от воркера обратно в плагин, кроме
`issueUrl` — канал односторонний.

## Контракт

Плагин отправляет JSON:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "reportId": "uuid",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-20T10:00:00.000Z",
  "pluginVersion": "0.0.5",
  "os": { "platform": "win32", "release": "10.0", "arch": "x64" },
  "node": "v22.0.0",
  "locale": "ru",
  "profile": "default",
  "taskName": "example",
  "description": "что сломалось",
  "contactEmail": "user@example.com",
  "redactedLogs": "…",
  "metrics": { "total": 10, "success": 8, "error": 2 },
  "website": ""
}
```

Ответы: `200 { "ok": true, "issueUrl": "https://github.com/…/issues/N" }`,
`400` при неверной схеме, `413` при слишком большом теле, `429` при
превышении лимита, `502` если GitHub недоступен/отверг запрос, `500` если
не задан `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Логи воркера не содержат PII — только `reportId`,
статус и код причины.

## Развёртывание (F-2.5)

1. Создайте fine-grained PAT с единственным правом **Issues: write** на
   `DeadSno/agent-steward` (Repository permissions → Issues → Read and write;
   остальное — None). Срок — минимально возможный.
2. Установите секрет **в два шага** (встречающаяся ошибка — вставить сам PAT
   в ответ на вопрос «Enter the name of your secret variable», тогда секрет
   сохраняется под именем токена, а воркер отвечает `500 receiver is not
   configured`):

   ```powershell
   npx wrangler secret put GITHUB_TOKEN
   # Enter the name of your secret variable: GITHUB_TOKEN
   # Enter a secret value: <вставьте PAT сюда>
   npx wrangler secret list   # в списке должно быть имя GITHUB_TOKEN
   ```

3. KV-привязки по умолчанию отключены: воркер использует in-memory хранилища
   для дедупа по `reportId` и rate-limit по IP (сбрасываются при рестарте
   изолята). Для персистентности создайте пространства и раскомментируйте
   блоки `[[kv_namespaces]]` в `wrangler.toml`, подставив выданные ID:

   ```powershell
   npx wrangler kv namespace create FEEDBACK_DEDUP
   npx wrangler kv namespace create FEEDBACK_RATELIMIT
   ```
4. Деплой: `npx wrangler deploy`. Скопируйте публичный URL.
5. В плагине: **Settings → Обратная связь с автором** → включить, вставить
   URL вида `https://agent-steward-feedback.<account>.workers.dev/report`.

Проверка перед включением:

```bash
curl -X POST "$URL" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"schemaVersion":1,"reportId":"probe-0001","createdAt":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","pluginVersion":"probe","os":{"platform":"test"},"node":"v22","description":"probe"}'
```

> На Windows с устаревшим Schannel `curl`/Node по умолчанию выбирают TLS 1.2 и
> получают от `*.workers.dev` `SSL alert 40`. В таком случае форсируйте TLS 1.3:
> `curl --tlsv1.3 …` либо в Node `https.request(..., { minVersion: 'TLSv1.3' })`.
> Это ограничение локального клиента, не воркера.

Живая проверка 20.11.2026: `POST /report` → `200` и
`https://github.com/DeadSno/agent-steward/issues/6`
(метки `user-report`, `needs-triage`).

## Приватность

- по умолчанию логи **не** прикладываются (`includeLogs: false`);
- клиент вырезает токены (`sk-`, `ghp_`, `xox*`, bot tokens), значения из
  `manage_secrets`, домашний путь → `~` и email → `[EMAIL]`;
- `contactEmail` отправляется только если пользователь указал его явно;
- `website` — honeypot против ботов: заполненное поле даёт молчаливый `200`
  без создания issue;

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-13

### Added

- **Full agent parity:** `schedule_task` now accepts `qualityGate`, `dependsOn`, `retryCount`, `retryDelay`, `nextTaskOnSuccess`, `nextTaskOnError` and the complete matrix configuration (`concurrency`, `overrides`).
- **New agent tools:** `update_task` (partial update, `matrix: null` removes the matrix), `pause_task`, `resume_task`, `get_history`, `get_task_logs`, `dry_run`, `manage_workspaces` (list/add/update/delete) and `matrix_control` (results/cancel/cleanup). 12 tools total.
- Agent tool descriptions are in English; runtime messages stay localized.
- `get_task_logs` supports a `lines` limit (1–1000).
- `update_task` keeps every field that is not passed, so the agent can change one setting without resending the whole task.
- **Built-in agent skill** `scheduled-job-best-practices`, registered by the plugin itself: guidance on schedule design, prompt structure, safety defaults, matrix concurrency, DAG rules and failure diagnosis, plus `references/recipes.md` with eight complete examples. No manual `.opencode/skills` setup.
- **Documentation:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (process model, modules, backends, data model, security model), `docs/FEATURES.md` (full feature catalog with examples and limits) and `docs/MIGRATION.md` (from cron, systemd timers, launchd and Windows Task Scheduler), linked from both READMEs.
- `test-docs.mjs` - 30 checks that the guides exist, stay complete and ship in the npm package.
- **History retention:** `history.retentionDays` (default 30) and `history.maxRecords` (default 5000) in settings (`0` disables either limit); daily auto-cleanup on plugin start plus `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum`; `cleanup_history` RPC and a «🧹 История и ретеншн» panel in the GUI with last-cleanup stats and an «Очистить сейчас» button.
- **14-day analytics:** `get_analytics` RPC and `GET /api/analytics` (runs, success rate, tokens, cost per day/task/model/matrix); dashboard «📊 Аналитика за период» block (KPIs, daily bar chart, top tasks by cost, matrices); history export to CSV/JSON (`GET /api/history/export?format=csv|json`) — `recordCost` falls back to a token-based estimate when `costUsd` is missing.
- **`/api/health`** now reports `version` (from package.json), `scheduler` (backend title), `queueDepth` (unfinished runs) and `db` status.
- `test-retention.mjs` - 19 checks; `test-metrics.mjs` - 25 checks; both wired into `npm test`.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-11-13

First public release.

### Added

- **Scheduling:** cron expressions registered with the native OS scheduler (Windows Task Scheduler, launchd, crontab), pause/resume, timeouts with hard kill, retries with delay, lock-file no-overlap protection.
- **Quality and lifecycle:** Quality Gate command, before/after scripts, allowed/denied tool lists, crash recovery for interrupted runs.
- **Orchestration:** `dependsOn` DAG, `nextTaskOnSuccess` / `nextTaskOnError` chains, file and MCP event triggers.
- **Matrix builds:** fan-out into `<parent>-matrix-<workspace>` clones, parallel/sequential strategies, `continue`/`stop` failure modes, per-matrix concurrency, per-workspace overrides, aggregator task, family sync on edit, cascade delete, cancel, orphan cleanup, `partial` status.
- **Workspaces:** multi-repo registry with path validation, per-task working directory and tool scoping.
- **Observability:** SQLite history and metrics, per-task logs, local web dashboard with pipeline view, matrix grouping and workspace summaries.
- **Operations:** dry-run preview, export/import JSON, templates, webhook notifications, settings.
- **Interfaces:** OpenCode sidebar GUI, web dashboard, agent tools `schedule_task`, `list_tasks`, `delete_task`, `run_task_now`.
- **Cross-platform:** scheduler abstraction with Windows, Linux and macOS backends.

### Known limitations

- Matrix parents are started by `runMatrix()` / DAG only; they are not cron-scheduled.
- Deleting a matrix parent deletes its family, but deleting a workspace does not touch existing matrix jobs.
- ~~Agent tools cover a subset of the RPC surface (see roadmap item 0.4).~~ Resolved in 1.1.0 (Full agent parity); extended to 29 tools with full RPC parity in the current dev line (`Unreleased`).

# Contributing

Thanks for taking the time to contribute! This project is MIT-licensed and free forever; contributions of code, docs, bug reports and recipes are welcome.

## Ways to help

- **Bug reports** — open an issue with OS, Node version, plugin version, steps to reproduce and the relevant log excerpt.
- **Feature requests** — describe the workflow you want to automate, not only the feature. See [ROADMAP-STRATEGY.md](ROADMAP-STRATEGY.md) for the direction.
- **Docs and recipes** — English docs are primary; Russian docs live in `docs/README.ru.md` and must stay in sync.
- **Code** — see below.

## Development setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/DeadSno/agent-steward.git
cd agent-steward
npm install
npm run build        # tsc
npm run build:gui    # vite -> gui-experimental.cjs
npm test             # all test suites
```

Requirements: Node.js 20+ (CI uses 24), npm 10+.

## Project layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/index.ts` | plugin lifecycle, agent tools, RPC handlers |
| `src/rpc.ts` | RPC contract schemas |
| `src/gui.tsx` | OpenCode sidebar panel (SolidJS) |
| `src/server.ts` | local web dashboard |
| `src/core/scheduler/` | OS scheduler backends (Windows, Linux, macOS) |
| `src/core/matrix.ts` | matrix fan-out, aggregation, sync, cancel |
| `src/core/record-history.ts` | history, retries, chains, matrix continuation |
| `src/db/` | SQLite storage (tasks, history, metrics, settings, templates) |
| `src/task-transfer.ts` | export, import, validation |

## Tests

Every change should keep the full suite green:

```bash
npm test
```

Individual suites: `npm run test:sqlite`, `test:crash`, `test:workspaces`, `test:role`, `test:dry-run`, `test:matrix`, `test:matrix-lifecycle`, `test:matrix-sync`, `test:agent`, `test:skill`, `test:docs`.

Tests run against `dist/`, so build first. They point `OPENCODE_SCHEDULER_HOME` (and legacy `APPDATA`) at a temporary directory, so they never touch your real jobs on any platform.

New behavior needs a test. Matrix sync and DAG logic are the most sensitive areas — cover both the happy path and the "running clone must not be touched" path.

## Code style

- TypeScript strict mode; no `any` unless there is no alternative.
- Keep platform-specific code inside `src/core/scheduler/` — everything else must stay cross-platform.
- No new runtime dependencies without an issue and a rationale (the project values a small dependency tree).
- User-facing strings in Russian are currently used by the GUI; new agent-tool descriptions and docs must be English-first.
- Follow the existing naming and file structure instead of introducing parallel abstractions.

## Pull requests

1. Fork, create a topic branch (`feat/matrix-retry`, `fix/launchd-weekday`).
2. Make focused commits with clear messages (`feat: ...`, `fix: ...`, `docs: ...`, `test: ...`).
3. Run `npm run build && npm run build:gui && npm test`.
4. Describe the problem, the solution and how you verified it; include screenshots for UI changes.
5. Update `CHANGELOG.md` (the next release section) and keep English/Russian docs in sync. New UI strings go to both `locales/ru.json` and `locales/en.json`; run `npm run test:en` when touching text.

CI runs build, GUI build and tests on Windows, Ubuntu and macOS for every pull request.

## Release process

**Do NOT run `npm publish` locally.** Releases are published exclusively by pushing a version tag (`git tag v1.5.6 && git push origin v1.5.6`), which triggers `.github/workflows/release.yml`. The release workflow:

1. Verifies `package.json` version matches the tag.
2. Runs `npm run build`, `npm run build:gui` and `npm test`.
3. Publishes to npm via OIDC trusted publishing with `--provenance` (no `NPM_TOKEN` secret required).
4. Creates a GitHub release.

Publishing is gated on two conditions: the event must be a `push` and the ref must be a `v*` tag. A manual `workflow_dispatch` run therefore never publishes: it executes the same verify matrix followed by `npm pack --dry-run` (dry-run job), which checks the manifest and the packaged tarball without touching the registry. Write permissions (`contents: write`, `id-token: write`) are granted only to the publish job; every other job runs with `contents: read`.

Use `npm version patch|minor|major` to bump the version before tagging.

# Cross-platform: Windows → macOS → Linux

The plugin is no longer tied to `schtasks`. The scheduler is an abstract layer with
three implementations, and run wrappers are generated for the target OS.

Translations: [Русский](docs/CROSS_PLATFORM.ru.md) · [中文](docs/CROSS_PLATFORM.zh.md)

## Architecture

```
src/
  index.ts                     # tools, RPC, plugin lifecycle
  gui.tsx                      # GUI panel (title comes from RPC)
  server.ts                    # web dashboard (dynamic title)
  core/
    scheduler/
      types.ts                 # SchedulerBackend, CreateTaskOptions, RunTaskResult
      index.ts                 # factory createSchedulerBackend() + getSchedulerTitle()
      windows.ts               # WindowsScheduler  (schtasks)
      linux.ts                 # LinuxScheduler    (crontab)
      mac.ts                   # MacScheduler      (launchd / LaunchAgents)
      posix.ts                 # shared base for Linux/macOS (task registry)
      registry.ts              # persistent task registry for POSIX backends
      logs.ts                  # cross-platform task log reader
    wrappers/
      bash.ts                  # .sh wrapper generator for Linux/macOS
    ps-wrapper.ts              # .ps1/.cmd wrappers for Windows (unchanged)
    record-history.ts          # metrics/history + retry/chains (via backend)
    cron-to-schtasks.ts        # cron → schtasks (Windows only)
```

### Interface

```ts
interface SchedulerBackend {
  readonly platform: NodeJS.Platform;
  readonly title: string;              // "Windows Task Scheduler" / "OpenCode Scheduler"
  createTask(options: CreateTaskOptions): Promise<void>;
  deleteTask(name: string): Promise<void>;
  runTask(name: string): Promise<RunTaskResult>;
  listTasks(): Promise<ScheduledTaskInfo[]>;
  pauseTask(name: string): Promise<void>;
  resumeTask(name: string): Promise<void>;
}
```

The factory picks an implementation from `process.platform`:
`win32 → WindowsScheduler`, `darwin → MacScheduler`, everything else → `LinuxScheduler`.

## How each OS works

### Windows (behaviour unchanged)
- Tasks are registered in Windows Task Scheduler via `schtasks` under `\OpenCode\agent-steward\` (profiles use `\OpenCode\agent-steward-<profile>\`). The legacy `\OpenCode\windows-scheduler\` folder is still read, renamed and deleted on demand.
- Wrapper: `run-task.ps1` plus a per-task `run-<name>.cmd` in `%APPDATA%\opencode\agent-steward\wrapper`. The legacy `%APPDATA%\opencode\windows-scheduler` directory is migrated on first start.
- Logs: `%APPDATA%\opencode\agent-steward\logs\<name>.log`.
- cron is converted to schtasks (`convertCronToSchTasks`) — the same pattern set as before.
- The prompt is passed to `opencode run` after `--`, so a prompt beginning with `-`
  cannot be mistaken for a flag. The wrapper rejects prompts longer than 30 000
  characters before `CreateProcess` (32 767-char command-line limit).
- Timeout watchdog: the process tree is read with `Get-CimInstance`; if CIM fails or
  returns nothing, the wrapper falls back to `Get-WmiObject`, then checks
  `tasklist`/`Get-Process`. If no tree data is available it fails closed and runs
  `taskkill /F /T /PID <root>`, so grandchildren are not left running.

### Linux
- Tasks live in a managed `crontab` block:
  ```
  # >>> opencode-scheduler:agent-steward >>>
  # task: my-task
  */5 * * * * /bin/bash '/…/wrapper/run-my-task.sh' >> '/…/logs/my-task.log' 2>&1
  # <<< opencode-scheduler:agent-steward <<<
  ```
  Legacy blocks without the `:<folder>` suffix are still read and removed.
- Pause = a line prefixed with `# PAUSED: ` (the block is rebuilt from the registry).
- Tasks with a `file` trigger never reach crontab — the plugin's FileWatchManager starts them.
- Wrapper: `~/.config/opencode/agent-steward/wrapper/run-<name>.sh` (chmod 0755).
- Full cron syntax (unlike Windows), because crontab understands it natively.
- One-shot (`once`): `at -t`; if `at` is not installed, the plugin falls back to a detached `sleep && command` process (`pid:<pid>` in the registry). The fallback does not survive a reboot — install the `at` package for durable one-shot runs.
- Delete/rebuild touches only its own block; other `crontab` lines are left alone.
- An unclosed plugin block (begin marker without end) fails closed: the plugin reports an error and does not rewrite the crontab, so user lines after the marker are never lost.

### macOS
- Tasks are LaunchAgent plists at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.opencode.scheduler.<name>.plist`.
- Schedule: `StartInterval` for `* * * * *` and `*/N`, `StartCalendarInterval` for `M * * * *`,
  `M H * * *`, `M H * * D`.
- Pause = `launchctl unload -w`, resume = `launchctl load -w`.
- Installing a paused task writes the plist but never calls `load -w` (it would
  clear the pause); `unload -w` keeps the agent disabled after the next login.
- `launchctl load` failures are not swallowed: the install/resume error carries
  the command, exit code and stderr (e.g. `Invalid property list` for a broken plist).
- Wrapper is the same `.sh` as on Linux; config paths:
  `~/.config/opencode/agent-steward/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`).

### Shared POSIX wrapper (`.sh`)
- `cd` into the working directory, `opencode run` with the prompt read from a file.
  The prompt follows `--`, so a leading `-` is not treated as an option.
- The argv backstop rejects `PROMPT_BYTES >= 131072`: Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`
  includes the trailing NUL, so at most 131 071 payload bytes fit.
- Logs are appended with `>>` and prefixed with timestamps.
- Locking via atomic `mkdir` — protects against parallel runs.
- Lock owner is written as `<pid>-<iso>` by Node/PS/bash; legacy `<iso>|<pid>` (PS)
  and bare `<pid>` are still read, so a live lock is never evicted by another runtime.
- On startup the plugin reads the owner of both `<task>.lock` and `<task>.lock.d/pid`:
  a lock directory is evicted only when its PID is dead or missing; age is a fallback.
- Timeout: child process + watchdog (`TERM`, then `KILL`).
- Quality Gate: `bash -lc "<command>"` (the `cmd.exe /c` equivalent on Windows).
- Metrics: `node "<record-history.js>" <task> <status> <started> <duration> <error> "-" "-"` —
  the same contract as the PowerShell wrapper, so history/metrics/retry/chains work everywhere.
- `PATH` is extended with `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.bun/bin`.

## Feature matrix

| Capability | Windows | Linux | macOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scheduler backend | `schtasks` | `crontab` | `launchd` LaunchAgents |
| Native cron subset | `* * * * *`, `*/N * * * *` (N ≤ 1439, 60 % N = 0), `M * * * *`, `M H * * *`, `M H * * D` | full cron | same subset as Windows |
| Other cron expressions | minute-poll + schedule gate | native cron | minute-poll + schedule gate |
| `*/N` in day-of-month / day-of-week | not native → poll | native | not native → poll |
| Pause / resume | `schtasks /change /disable` / `/enable` | `# PAUSED:` line in the managed block | `launchctl unload -w` / `load -w` |
| File triggers | in-process `FileWatchManager` | same | same |
| Task wrappers | `.cmd` + `.ps1` | `.sh` | `.sh` |
| Logs | `%APPDATA%\opencode\agent-steward\logs` | `~/.config/opencode/agent-steward/logs` | same as Linux |
| `secrets.key` protection | `icacls` (owner only) + `chmod` fallback | `chmod 0600` | `chmod 0600` |
| Dashboard | `127.0.0.1`, dynamic title | same | same |
| DAG / matrix / quality gates / notifications | in-plugin, OS-independent | same | same |

### Compromises

1. **Minute-poll.** Cron expressions outside the native subset, and tasks with a non-system
   IANA time zone, are started every minute by the OS scheduler; `schedule-gate` decides
   whether the run proceeds. The cost is one short-lived wrapper process per task per minute.
2. **`M H */N * *` is deliberately not converted to `schtasks /sc DAILY /mo N`.**
   Cron counts days from the 1st of each month and resets at month boundaries; `/mo N`
   counts days from the task creation date and does not reset. The two schedules are not
   equivalent, so the expression stays in poll mode. A native variant would require
   `MONTHLY` with an explicit `/d` list, not `DAILY /mo N`.
3. **DST.** The gate works with local wall-clock time. A nonexistent time (spring forward)
   is skipped; an ambiguous time (fall back) runs at the first occurrence.
4. **`*/N * * * *` on Windows** is native only when `60 % N = 0` and `N ≤ 1439`.
   Otherwise the task falls back to poll mode, because `schtasks /mo N` counts from the
   creation moment while cron counts from the start of the hour.
5. **POSIX wrappers, crontab and launchd have not been executed on real Linux/macOS hosts**
   (see Limitations); syntax and escaping are covered by tests only.

## GUI and dashboard
- The title is dynamic: "Windows Task Scheduler" on Windows, "OpenCode Scheduler" on macOS/Linux.
- The title comes from the `get_platform` RPC method → `{ platform, title }`.
- The title is used in the GUI panel, in the error fallback panel, and in the dashboard `<title>/<h1>`.
- Buttons, statuses, tables, DAG and metrics do not depend on the OS.
- Tool descriptions (`schedule_task` and others) substitute the actual scheduler name.

## Build and checks
- `npm run build` — OK, no errors.
- `npm run build:gui` — OK (`gui-experimental.cjs`, ~47.7 kB).
- Verified at runtime:
  - titles for win32/darwin/linux;
  - `cronToLaunchdSchedule` on several expressions;
  - live `listTasks()` on Windows — tasks come back with short names (no prefix);
  - `shellQuote` escaping (quotes, spaces, Cyrillic);
  - `dist/index.js` imports fine, `dist` does not pull `schtasks.js` directly.

## Limitations and what to verify on real machines
1. `.sh` wrappers and crontab/launchd were **never executed** — the current Windows box has no
   `bash`/WSL. Syntax and escaping were checked by hand; a run on Linux and macOS is still needed.
2. cron → launchd supports the same limited pattern set as Windows
   (`* * * * *`, `*/N * * * *`, `M * * * *`, `M H * * *`, `M H * * D`).
   Linux gets full cron.
3. The Windows task prefix is now `\OpenCode\agent-steward\` (legacy `\OpenCode\windows-scheduler\` is still recognized); the plugin id is kept for backwards compatibility.
4. `src/schtasks.ts` remains as a thin shim for old scripts (`test-create.cjs`, `test-run.cjs`);
   all logic now lives in `core/scheduler/windows.ts`.

# 🎯 Стратегический роадмап — agent-steward

> Цель: **стать лучшим фреймворком-супервизором для OpenCode, оставаясь бесплатным и open source.**  
> North Star: [docs/CONCEPT.md](./docs/CONCEPT.md) — верифицируемая локально-первая оркестрация агент-задач.  
> Тактический спринт-план — в [ROADMAP.md](./ROADMAP.md), выпущенные изменения — в [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md).

---

## Позиционирование

**Мы не «cron для OpenCode». Мы не «плагин-планировщик».**  
Scheduler, уведомления, аналитика — триггеры и обвязка, не ядро (CONCEPT §8).

Мы — **локальная платформа оркестрации AI-задач**: расписание + зависимости (DAG) + матрицы (fan-out) + политики качества + наблюдаемость + объективный гейт + learning-loop.

| Принцип | Что это значит на практике |
|---------|---------------------------|
| **Бесплатно навсегда** | MIT, без SaaS, без телеметрии, без «pro»-функций |
| **Локально по умолчанию** | Control plane, данные, история, логи, аудит — на машине пользователя |
| **Open source-first** | Публичный roadmap, CI на 3 ОС, английская документация |
| **Оркестрация, а не таймер** | Ров — DAG, матрицы, Quality Gates, наблюдаемость. Cron скопируют за неделю |

## Стратегия развития: от плагина к фреймворку (CONCEPT §13)

Наша эволюция строится на двух столпах и постепенной абстракции.

### Этап 1: глубокая интеграция с OpenCode V1 и V2 (текущий, завершён milestone Д7)

Один пакет, dual export, общее ядро `createRuntime`. V1 и V2 работают через один и тот же пакет с разными ключами конфига (`plugin` для V1, `plugins` для V2).

Статус: ✅ завершён — `agent-steward@0.0.2` опубликован, старый пакет остаётся как `legacy/` (thin re-export на один major).

### Этап 2: абстракция слоя исполнения (Agent Executor Interface)

Вынести интерфейс исполнителя агента за пределы OpenCode-specific кода. Позволить запускать задачи не только через OpenCode, но и через других агентов / MCP / стандартные API.

Планируемые спринты: 38 (Approvals, окружения, артефакты, 0.1.0). Спринт 32 (Pipeline-as-code) и спринт 36 (Durable DAG) уже выполнены: выпущены в 0.0.5 / 0.0.3–0.0.4 (см. CHANGELOG).

### Этап 3: универсальный фреймворк оркестрации (долгосрочно, 0.2.x+)

Универсальный фреймворк, совместимый с любым агентом через MCP или стандартные API. Контекстные артефакты, роли (worker → reviewer), self-correcting retry, model fallback chain, A/B tournament, CEP, входящие внешние события, cross-run memory.

Планируемые спринты: 40–47 (Context artifacts, Crew / роли, Self-correcting retry, Model fallback, Tournament, CEP, входящие события, Cross-run memory, Smart recipes).

## Ров, который не скопируют за неделю

1. **Windows-супервизия.** Конкурент `opencode-scheduler` прямо предупреждает, что на Windows не гарантирует no-overlap и таймауты; у нас обёртки, lock-файлы, crash recovery и единая модель на трёх ОС.
2. **OpenCode v2.** Часть плагинов всё ещё на устаревшем конфиге `plugin` и не подтверждает совместимость с v2.
3. **Оркестрация.** DAG, матрицы, Quality Gates, `partial`-статусы, dry-run и история — этого нет ни у одного планировщика экосистемы.
4. **Локальность.** Никаких облаков и аккаунтов — конкуренты с SaaS-моделью сюда не пойдут.
5. **Learning-loop.** Capability-карта + gate-passed датасет + staged LoRA-адаптеры — персональная компандующаяся capability, которой нет ни у облака, ни у OpenCode core, ни у swarm-фреймворков.

**Чего не делаем:** свой sandbox, свою CI-платформу, хостинг агентов, платные тарифы, open-ended AGI-swarm (CONCEPT §8).

# 4. Правила работы (канбан)

1. **Одна подзадача за раз.** Взял → сделал → отчёт → следующая подзадача.
2. **Слой не пропускается.** Деталь → задача → подзадача; подзадача закрывается только с тестом и документацией.
3. **Закрытое уходит из ROADMAP.** Выполненная задача/подзадача удаляется отсюда и попадает в CHANGELOG.
4. **Нет спринтов.** Статусы ⬜ → 🔄 → ✅ независимо от релизов.
5. **Версия — следствие релиза, а не обещание.** `npm version` в момент релиза.
6. **Приоритет — по боли пользователя.** P1 = без этого нельзя рекомендовать плагин.
7. **Fail-open по умолчанию.** Необязательная подсистема при отказе деградирует, а не блокирует.
8. **Сверка с CONCEPT.md.** Четыре столпа (§4), без противоречий §8.
9. **Честность в маркетинге.** Оценки — с методикой рядом.

# Security Policy

## Supported versions

| Version | Supported |
|---|---|
| 0.0.x | ✅ |
| < 0.0 | ❌ |

## Threat model — read this first

`agent-steward` is a **local automation tool**. By design it:

- registers jobs with the operating system scheduler;
- generates wrapper scripts that execute `opencode run` with a prompt;
- runs user-provided `beforeScript`, `afterScript` and Quality Gate commands through the system shell;
- stores job definitions, history and logs on the local machine.

Therefore:

1. **Job definitions are code.** Anyone who can create or edit a job can execute arbitrary commands under your user account. Protect the config directory and review imported job files (`.json`) before importing.
2. **The web dashboard is local.** Do not expose its port to untrusted networks; it has no authentication layer.
3. **Secrets** (`${secret:NAME}`) are scoped to the fields where they are actually used and masked in logs/outputs. Secret masking is enforced; prefer environment variables managed outside the plugin for additional isolation.
4. **Tool allow/deny lists are enforced** by the runtime wrappers, not just metadata. They do not replace OS-level isolation. Background jobs default to the `hybrid` permission policy: `shell` and `question` are denied unless the job explicitly lists them in `allowedTools` (or sets the transitional `legacyShell: true`). See [`README.md` → Permissions](README.md#permissions).
5. **Dashboard mutations** (run, delete, cancel-matrix, matrix-cleanup) require a trusted source. The source check is **Origin-first**: a request with an `Origin` header is trusted only when that origin is loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`); a request without `Origin` is trusted only when its `Host` is loopback. The custom `X-Scheduler-Client` header is additional confirmation and **does not bypass** this check — an external or `null` Origin is rejected even when the header is present. The port is bound to loopback only; do not expose it to untrusted networks.
6. **Encryption keys on Windows.** `secrets.key` gets mode `0600` on POSIX. Windows ignores POSIX modes, so the plugin applies a restrictive ACL with `icacls` (`/inheritance:r` and a single full-control grant for the current user). This is best-effort: if `icacls` fails, a warning is logged and the key remains protected only by the default profile ACL. The same protection is applied to existing keys on first load after an upgrade.
7. **Background jobs run with `--auto`.** Permission rules are generated per job and passed through `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`; they are not a sandbox. Treat every job definition as code and review imported jobs.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please **do not open a public issue** for security problems.

- Use GitHub Security Advisories: <https://github.com/DeadSno/agent-steward/security/advisories/new>
- Include: affected version, OS, reproduction steps, impact and a suggested fix if you have one.

You can expect an acknowledgement within 72 hours and a coordinated disclosure timeline. Reporters will be credited in the release notes unless they prefer otherwise.

## Scope

In scope: command injection through job fields, path traversal in export/import, unsafe wrapper generation, credential leakage in logs, privilege issues in the OS scheduler integration, dashboard exposure.

Out of scope: issues that require an already-compromised local account, and the intentional ability to run arbitrary shell commands through job definitions.

# План тестирования плагина `agent-steward` (plugin id `opencode-windows-scheduler`)

**Версия плагина:** 0.0.6 · **Платформа прогона:** Windows 11 · **Дата:** 20.11.2026  
**Объект:** весь плагин — ядро, MCP-инструменты, GUI OpenCode, веб-дашборд, TUI, БД, интеграции, локальный ассистент триажа, самодиагностика, DLQ, durable-запуски, pipeline-as-code.  
**Цель:** доказать три свойства для каждой детали:

1. подсистема работает (функционально и на ошибках);
2. у агента есть доступ к подсистеме (MCP-инструмент или документированный обходной путь);
3. пользователь может сделать то же самое через GUI/дашборд/TUI, а результат совпадает.

> **100% покрытие:** каждая деталь (D01–D18) содержит не только «счастливый путь», но и ошибки, граничные значения, узкие места, планы улучшений и доработки. Подзадачи с префиксом `Sxx.BP.*` — это проверка «узких мест / багов / улучшений / доработок» и обязательны для приёмки детали.

## 9. Модель выполнения: агент параллельно с человеком

Принцип: **каждая функция проверяется двумя дорожками** — агентом через MCP и пользователем через GUI/дашборд/TUI. Если пользователь не хочет или не может выполнить шаг вручную, агент выполняет его от его имени, и результат должен быть идентичным.

| Дорожка | Кто выполняет | Инструмент | Что проверяется |
|---|---|---|---|
| Агент | MCP-агент | 30 инструментов из §1 | Все инструменты вызываются, схемы валидируют аргументы, ошибки структурированы |
| Пользователь | Человек | GUI OpenCode, веб-дашборд, TUI | Кнопки, настройки, формы, дашборд — работают и дают тот же результат |
| Паритет | Агент + человек параллельно | Любая операция (create → run → read → delete) | Состояние совпадает во всех интерфейсах, аудит содержит корректный actor |

**Правило:** после завершения любой задачи (создание задачи, изменение настроек, запуск матрицы, тест триажа и т.д.) агент и человек сверяют результат: `list_tasks` (агент) = таблица GUI = дашборд. Если расходятся — дефект.

# Architecture

This document explains how `agent-steward` (plugin id
`opencode-windows-scheduler`) is put together: the process
model, the modules, the data model and the extension points.

- [Design principles](#design-principles)
- [Process model](#process-model)
- [Data flow](#data-flow)
- [Modules](#modules)
- [Scheduling backends](#scheduling-backends)
- [Run wrapper](#run-wrapper)
- [History, metrics and recovery](#history-metrics-and-recovery)
- [Chains, retries and DAG](#chains-retries-and-dag)
- [Matrix builds](#matrix-builds)
- [Workspaces](#workspaces)
- [Triggers](#triggers)
- [Storage](#storage)
- [Interfaces](#interfaces)
- [Localization](#localization)

## Design principles

1. **The OS scheduler owns time.** The plugin never keeps a timer in memory for cron
   jobs. Every recurring task becomes a real OS entry (Task Scheduler, launchd,
   crontab), so jobs survive reboots and closed editor windows.
2. **The host process owns the UI.** Agent tools, the sidebar GUI, the RPC layer and the
   dashboard live inside the OpenCode plugin host. They are stateless wrappers around
   the database and the OS scheduler.
3. **Runs are independent processes.** A job executes `opencode run` through a wrapper
   that enforces timeout, single-instance locking, pre/post hooks and a Quality Gate.
   The wrapper reports the result back to the database, not to the plugin host.
4. **One source of truth for definitions is SQLite.** OS entries are derived artifacts:
   they can always be recreated from the database with export/import.
5. **Local first.** No network services, no telemetry, no accounts by default. The dashboard binds
   to localhost only. Local AI triage (Ollama) is optional and connects only when explicitly enabled
   via `manage_local_ai`.

## Execution model

agent-steward is an execution engine with optional trigger registration — not a
scheduler with extras attached. Four kinds of entry lead into the same execution
path, and the OS scheduler is only one of them (CONCEPT §5, §8):

| Entry | Examples | Goes through the OS scheduler? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ad-hoc (no OS registration) | GUI · CLI · TUI · RPC (`run_mission`) | No |
| internal orchestration (core-driven, no OS) | chains · DAG dependents · retries · matrix continuation · escalation · resume after pause/crash | No |
| registered triggers | `cron` / `once` | Yes — registered with Task Scheduler / launchd / crontab |
| registered, in-process | `file` / `git` / `mcp-event` / webhook | No — watched inside the plugin process |

Orchestration (chains, DAG, retries, matrix, escalation) is performed by the core
and the recorder through **direct wrapper launches**, never by the OS scheduler.
The OS scheduler is responsible only for firing registered `cron`/`once` ticks.

```
                  │  • one-shot cleanup (Windows) ─▶ OS scheduler    │
                  │  • notifications: webhook / Telegram / toasts    │
                  │    (+ async triage, optional local model)        │
                  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| Process | Lifetime | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plugin host | OpenCode session | agent tools and RPC; sidebar GUI and TUI; dashboard HTTP server (UI, `/api/*` with origin guard, `/api/hooks` HMAC, `/metrics`); in-process triggers (chokidar file watcher, git polling, MCP events, webhook ingestion); durable-run executor (resume / pause / DLQ); startup recovery |
| OS scheduler | system service | optional lane for `cron`/`once` ticks only: Task Scheduler (Windows), launchd (macOS), crontab + `at` (Linux; detached `sleep` fallback when `at` is unavailable) |
| Run wrapper | one per run | the single execution unit; direct launches and registered ticks execute the same wrapper, so direct runs get the same gate, lock, timeout, hooks and policy |
| schedule-gate | seconds, child of the wrapper | separate `node` process; exit 3 = "not now" (skip or postpone), fail-closed on invalid cron |
| recorder | seconds, one per run | short-lived `node` process started by the wrapper with `--start` / `--finish`; independent of the plugin host |

### Why direct launches are safe

A common question: does `run_task_now` / chain continuation skip the safety
machinery? No. Both lanes converge on the same wrapper, so every direct run still
passes through the schedule gate, takes the lock, runs under the timeout watchdog,
loads env/secrets with the task permission policy, and records history through the
recorder. The only difference is *who starts the wrapper*: the OS scheduler or the
core.

### Unified execution path (AC-1)

`src/core/execution.ts` is the single core path for both registered tasks and
ad-hoc missions: `createRun → plan → route → execute → GATE → ledger`. The origin
(`registered` or `ad-hoc`) changes where the context comes from, not what happens
next.

- **`RunContext` (AC-1.1)** — entry, trigger, task name, mission/prompt, cwd,
  profile (model, session policy, workspace) and safety contract (permission
  policy, allowed/denied tools). `createRegisteredRunContext` builds it from a
  task definition; `createAdHocRunContext` from a free-form mission, defaulting
  to `ad-hoc` / `new` session / `hybrid` policy. `validateRunContext` rejects
  empty fields, unknown policies and tools listed as both allowed and denied.
- **Plan and dry-run trace (AC-1.3)** — `buildExecutionPlan` either uses the
  explicit task type or asks the heuristic planner to decompose the mission, then
  routes every step through the capability map. `describeExecutionPlan` prints the
  ordered steps, their local/cloud/review targets and routing source without
  creating a run row, so the same plan can be inspected before execution.
- **Executor abstraction (AC-1.2)** — `StepExecutor` advertises which routes it
  supports and receives `{ step, context, plan }`. `createOpenCodeExecutor`
  adapts the OpenCode CLI, but the core no longer depends on that transport:
  another executor can serve the same plan.
- **Execution and GATE (AC-1.4)** — `executeExecutionPlan` creates one ledger run,
  executes steps through the journal (so retries, leases and crash recovery still
  apply), calls the optional GATE after each result and stops on the first
  failure. Steps routed to review/explore are recorded as `skipped` with the
  routing reason instead of being silently dropped.

The test `test-execution-pipeline.mjs` drives a registered task and an ad-hoc
mission through the same executor, including a rejecting GATE and a skipped
review step.

### Ad-hoc mission runtime (AB-8)

`src/core/mission.ts` turns a one-off request into a `RunContext` without
registering anything in the OS scheduler. The same entry point is exposed by
the RPC method `run_mission` (not registered as an agent tool), the CLI command `agent-steward run`
and the GUI panel «Ad-hoc миссия».

- **MissionSpec (AB-8.1)** — `prompt` is required; `cwd`, `taskName`,
  `taskType`, `model`, `session` (`new` / `reuse` / `last`), `sessionId`,
  `timeoutSeconds` (1–86400), `gate`, `gateTimeoutSeconds`, `policy`
  (`hybrid` / `secure` / `legacy`), `allowedTools`, `deniedTools` and `dryRun`
  are optional. `normalizeMissionSpec` trims the prompt, makes `cwd` absolute,
  rejects unknown policies/timers/sessions and tools listed as both allowed and
  denied. The default task type is `mission`, routed statically to
  `local`/`direct`.
- **Safety contract** — the mission is a normal `RunContext` with its own
  permission policy and tool lists. It does not bypass the GATE, budget, audit
  or ledger; the wrapper receives the gate command and permission config just
  like a registered task. An in-process lock keyed by the resolved workspace
  rejects a second mission in the same directory
  (`В workspace … уже выполняется миссия …`).
- **Planning and dry-run** — `buildExecutionPlan` + `describeExecutionPlan`
  produce the same trace as registered runs. `dryRun: true` returns the plan
  with `status: "planned"` and does not create a ledger row.
- **Execution (AB-8.2/8.3)** — without an injected executor the mission writes
  the prompt file, log, lock and wrapper (`writeWrapperCmd` on Windows,
  `writeBashWrapper` on POSIX), spawns the wrapper with a hard timeout, and
  feeds its output into `executeExecutionPlan`; the run is stored with
  `metadata.adHoc = true` and tasks are never created in Windows Task Scheduler,
  launchd or crontab. An injected `StepExecutor` is used by tests and
  alternative transports.
- **Results** — `MissionResult` reports `success`, `dryRun`, `runId`, `status`
  (`planned` / `passed` / `failed`), `steps`, `error`, `logFile` and the
  human-readable plan description. `run_mission` returns the same data minus
  raw step output.

The test `test-mission-run.mjs` covers dry-run (no ledger row), a successful
ad-hoc run, executor failure, the workspace lock, input validation and a static
check that the mission path never imports the OS scheduler.

### Data: one SQLite per profile

Each profile has its own plugin directory, its own SQLite database, its own OS-task
namespace and its own dashboard port. `default` keeps 3782 (fallback 4782); a named
profile gets the first free port from 3783 upward when it is created, recorded in its
`profile.json`, and never one already reserved by `default` or another profile. Every
dashboard response carries `x-plugin-profile`, so a second profile neither reuses
another profile's server nor treats it as a zombie.

`SCHEMA_VERSION` is currently **12**; migrations are additive and idempotent,
applied through `PRAGMA user_version` on open. Step 11 adds functional indexes
`idx_history_task_lower` / `idx_history_status_lower` for `getHistory()` filters.

### Known limitations (execution)

- Startup recovery (`recoverInterrupted*`) marks unfinished rows as `error`; it
  does not yet check whether the wrapper process is still alive, so a plugin
  restart during a live run finalizes that run early (tracked: Trust hotfix).
- Durable steps currently execute through the same wrapper machinery; the
  agent-executor abstraction (run missions without an OpenCode-specific
  transport) is Stage 2 of the strategy (sprints 32/38).

## Run wrapper

The wrapper is generated per task and is the only place where execution policy is
enforced:

| Concern | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Working directory | Task `workingDirectory`, or the workspace path, or the plugin directory |
| Prompt | Written to a prompt file, passed to `opencode run` |
| Timeout | `timeoutSeconds`; on expiry the child process tree is stopped and the run is marked `timeout` (Windows: CIM → WMI → `tasklist`/`Get-Process`, fail-closed tree kill) |
| Workspace env | Variables from the workspace's `.env` file and explicit pairs are injected before `opencode run` (wrapper `env:` / `export`); secret-looking keys are masked in logs |
| No overlap | Lock file per task; a second start exits immediately and records `skipped` |
| Pre-flight | `beforeScript`; non-zero exit marks `preFlight` as failed |
| Quality Gate | `qualityGate` after a successful run; non-zero exit turns the run into an error |
| Post-flight | `afterScript`; non-zero exit is reported but does not rewrite a success |
| Logging | Append-only log per task under `logs/` |
| History | Calls the recorder with `--start` and `--finish` |

**Gate input and worktree snapshots.** A task with `qualityGate` stores a hash of
the gate command, prompt and timeout when it is created (`core/gate-integrity.ts`,
`gate-snapshots/*.json`); before the gate runs, both wrappers verify that hash and
fail closed on a mismatch (G-1.2). **PL-25:** a parallel agent can edit `src/`
without committing while a task is running, which used to make the start lint green
and the post-flight gate fail on somebody else's uncommitted code. The wrappers now
also capture a worktree snapshot at task start — `HEAD` plus
`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no -- src` — into a sibling
`*.worktree.json` file, and verify it immediately before the gate. Guard paths are
configurable via `AGENT_STEWARD_GATE_GUARD_PATHS` (separator `|` or `;`). If `HEAD`
or the guarded working tree changed during the run, the gate is skipped and the run
is marked as an error with an explicit message; non-git directories are not guarded.
This prevents a green gate from certifying code that was changed by another task.

**Единый формат lock-токена (B6).** Node (`src/core/lock.ts`), PowerShell
(`src/core/ps-wrapper.ts`) и bash (`src/core/wrappers/bash.ts`) используют один
формат записи владельца: `<pid>-<iso>` (Node добавляет `-<uuid>` для
уникальности токена). Все три стороны понимают и старые варианты:
`<iso>|<pid>` (legacy PowerShell), `<pid>-<epoch>-<uuid>` (legacy Node) и
голый `<pid>` из pid-файла bash. Общий парсер — `parseLockToken()` в Node,
`Get-LockOwnerPid` в PS и `parse_lock_pid` в bash — разбирает legacy
`<iso>|<pid>` до проверки `<pid>-…`: раньше год из ISO принимался за PID,
из-за чего живой lock вытеснялся. Перед своим каталогом `<lock>.d` bash
проверяет файловый lock Node/PS и не запускает задачу, если его владелец жив.
`test-lock-format.mjs` проверяет парсеры и interop в обе стороны.

**Вытеснение каталога `.lock.d` (B7).** При старте плагина `LockManager.initialize()`
читает владельца из `<task>.lock.d/pid` тем же парсером, что и `.lock`, и не
трогает каталог, пока процесс жив, — даже если он старше 24 ч (задача с
`timeoutSeconds: 0` может работать легально долго). Возраст остаётся только
fallback'ом: каталог без pid-файла или с мёртвым PID вытесняется атомарным
`rename` в `.stale-*`. Тест — `test-stale-lock.mjs` (живой PID сохраняется,
мёртвый и безымянный вытесняются).

Windows uses PowerShell and `.cmd` shims; POSIX uses bash. Both wrappers are generated
from templates so the policy stays identical across platforms.

## History, metrics and recovery

`history` stores one row per run: status (`running`, `success`, `error`, `timeout`,
`partial`), start/finish timestamps, duration, error text, tokens, cost, model,
pre/post-flight results, the chained next task, workspace and tool restrictions.
`metrics` holds per-task counters and totals.

Usage (tokens/cost) resolves in both recorder modes: explicit wrapper arguments win,
and when they are `-` the recorder parses the log tail (`parseUsageFromLog`) using the
log path passed as the last argument. This applies to `--finish` (12th argument) and to
the legacy pre-`--start` mode (11th argument, B10); a missing/unreadable log degrades to
the next source instead of failing the record. Many OpenCode providers (for example
hy4-flash-free and local Ollama) print no usage lines at all, so `parseUsageFromLog`
alone leaves tokens at zero. In that case `core/opencode-usage.ts` reads OpenCode's own
SQLite database read-only (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, override via
`OPENCODE_USAGE_DB`) and sums assistant-message `tokens`/`cost` from `message.data`
inside a ±2 s window around the run, optionally restricted to the task's working
directory. `record-history.ts` fills only fields that are still missing and emits a
`usage.from_opencode_db` structured event; a missing or locked database is ignored.
Offline tool-surface measurement lives in `core/usage-surface.ts`: it accepts an
injected tokenizer (the test uses `gpt-tokenizer`) so the reported size of the 30-tool
registry is a real token count, not a character heuristic.

If the host or the machine dies mid-run, the row stays in `running`. On the next
plugin activation, `db/recovery.ts` marks stale `running` rows as `error`, so the UI
never shows a permanently running task.

History is bounded by retention: `settings.json` carries `history.retentionDays` and
`history.maxRecords` (defaults 30 / 5000, `0` disables). Cleanup runs at most once a
day on plugin start (`core/retention.ts`), prunes only finished rows via
`pruneHistory` in `db/history-repo.ts`, then `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum` frees space.
Aggregates in `metrics` are never pruned. Period analytics (per-day buckets, success
rate, tokens, cost, matrix/model breakdowns) are computed by `core/analytics.ts` and
exposed as `get_analytics` / `GET /api/analytics`; the dashboard renders a 14-day
block and `GET /api/history/export` serves CSV/JSON.

## Chains, retries and DAG

All three are evaluated by the recorder after a run finishes:

- **Retries** — `retryCount`/`retryDelay` with a retry-state file so a crash cannot
  loop forever. Retries are attempted before chains and dependents.
- **Chains** — `nextTaskOnSuccess` / `nextTaskOnError` start exactly one follow-up task.
- **DAG** — `dependsOn` is satisfied only when every dependency's latest run is
  successful. For a matrix dependency, all clones must be successful; the parent's own
  aggregate record is not enough.

`selectDependentsToTrigger(taskName, definitions, history)` is a pure function, which
keeps the rules testable.

**Dependency completion is an event, not a one-shot latch (PL-40).** Every time a
dependency finishes, its completion is evaluated against the dependencies' latest
records. If all dependencies are currently successful, the dependent is started — even
when an earlier run of the same generation already started it. With two parents this
means the dependent may run once per parent completion (e

metadata is still recorded in history for audit.
- **Default policy (`src/core/permissions.ts`):** the baseline is
  `permissions.defaultPolicy` — `hybrid` (default) denies `shell` and `question` while
  allowing read/edit/glob/grep/subagent/skill/webfetch/websearch, `secure` allows only
  read/glob/grep/skill, `legacy` allows everything (1.5.x behaviour). Task `legacyShell`
  re-enables `shell` under `hybrid`; `deniedTools` still wins. Policy denials are
  audited as `tool.blocked` with `reason: "default-policy"`, and each wrapper logs
  `policy=<name>, denied=<actions>` before the run.
- **Audit of blocked tools (Sprint 29.4):** when a task definition is saved,
  `recordTaskToolBlocks()` writes one `tool.blocked` audit event per entry in
  `deniedTools` (`target` = task name, `details.tool` = tool, plus `allowedTools`,
  `deniedTools` and `reason`). In allow-list mode one event with `tool: "*"` records
  that every unlisted tool is denied. The event is emitted on create and on update, so
  changing the task policy also changes the audited details. Because the wrapper runs
  `opencode` as an external process, the plugin cannot observe individual blocked
  attempts at runtime; the audit reflects the enforced policy, not each refusal.
- Task prompts, hooks and Quality Gate scripts are **plain text** executed with your
  user privileges; only secrets (in `secrets.json`, AES-256-GCM) are encrypted.
  Workspace `env` can reference secrets as `${secret:NAME}`; values are masked in
  logs, history and audit. Treat task creation like granting shell access.
- Secrets are stored encrypted in `<PLUGIN_DIR>/secrets.json` (AES-256-GCM) with a
  32-byte key file `secrets.key` (mode 0600 on POSIX; on Windows an ACL that removes
  inheritance and grants the current user only, applied by `icacls` on create and
  re-applied on read for keys created before 1.5.5). Workspace `env` can reference them
  as `${secret:NAME}`; values are substituted at run time and masked in logs,
  history and audit.
- Workspace paths are validated, but hooks are not sandboxed: only schedule jobs from
  repositories you trust.

### Permission model

The effective policy is resolved in this order (later wins):

1. `permissions.defaultPolicy` — the baseline: `hybrid` (default, no `shell`/`question`),
   `secure` (read-only) or `legacy` (everything allowed, 1.5.x behaviour).
2. Task `legacyShell` — re-enables `shell` under `hybrid` only.
3. Task `allowedTools` — if present, every action not listed is denied; an explicitly
   listed action can override a policy denial.
4. Task `deniedTools` — always denied and takes priority over `allowedTools`.
5. The generated `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` — passed in the wrapper environment; no file
   is written and the project config stays untouched.
6. Project `opencode.json(c)` and system config — merged by OpenCode; a closer or
   system-level config can weaken task-scoped denies (see limitations below).
7. `--auto` — auto-approves everything that remains, so no interactive prompts block
   an unattended run.

Tool mapping used by both wrappers:

| Task tool | OpenCode action |
| --- | --- |
| `bash`, `shell` | `shell` |
| `write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, `remove` | `edit` |
| `glob`, `grep`, `webfetch`, `websearch` | same name |
| `question`, `subagent`, `skill` | same name |

Hooks, Quality Gates and wrapper scripts are outside this model: they run before or
after the agent with the user's privileges and are not filtered by tool policy.

### Permission enforcement — known limitations (spike 29.1 findings)

- `opencode run` CLI (v2.2.3) supports only `--auto` (auto-approve non-denied
  permissions). There are **no** `--allow-tool` / `--deny-tool` CLI flags, so
  per-task restrictions cannot be passed via arguments. Enforcement is done by
  generating a task-scoped config and passing it through `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`.
- OpenCode merges `opencode.json(c)` from the current directory up to the filesystem
  root. A project-level `opencode.jsonc` with permissive rules can override or weaken
  task-scoped denies (last matching rule wins, closer directory wins for merge).
  System config (`/etc/opencode`, `%ProgramData%\opencode`) overrides project config.
- Nested agent calls (subagents) use their **own** permissions, not a subset of the
  parent's. A task that denies `subagent` prevents launching subagents, but a launched
  subagent is not further restricted by the parent task's policy.
- **Plan B**: if the task-scoped config passed via `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` proves
  insufficient, enforcement can be moved to wrapper-level tool filtering (intercepting
  `opencode run` invocation and refusing to start when a denied tool would be needed)
  or to a managed system-level `policies` entry that hard-denies specific tools
  globally.

| RPC-методы (`get_platform` и др.) | **нет** | да | subpath `@opencode/plugin/rpc` в V1 отсутствует |
| HTTP-dashboard | да | да | не зависит от plugin API |
| DAG, matrix, gates, история, уведомления | да | да | общее ядро |
| SQLite-состояние | да | да | `<PLUGIN_DIR>/scheduler.db` |
| Ключ конфига | `plugin` | `plugins` | ключ своей линии; см. «Конфигурация по линиям» |

**Явно:** GUI и RPC — только V2. TUI — обе линии: `package.json` объявляет
`exports["./tui"] = "./src/tui.tsx"` (как в документации OpenCode для
пакетов-плагинов), а сам модуль отдаёт `{ ...v2Tui, tui: tuiV1 }`: V2 читает
`setup`, V1 — `tui`. Пакет не обещает GUI/RPC в V1 и не подменяет TUI-панель
заглушкой.

**Конфигурация по линиям.** Ключ выбирает загрузчик OpenCode, а не плагин: сам
пакет не читает ни `plugin`, ни `plugins`, поэтому чужое поле не может уронить
его код. V1 подключается ключом `plugin` в `opencode.jsonc`, V2 — ключом
`plugins` или командой `opencode plugin add agent-steward`. Оба
ключа одновременно не нужны. Примеры для обеих линий — в README (en/ru/zh).

**TUI в V1.** `src/tui-v1.tsx` реализует `TuiPluginModule` и живёт на тех же
данных, что V2: `getJobsView`, `groupJobsForDisplay`, `statusIcon`,
`formatJobLog`. Возможности V1 TUI:

- маршрут `/scheduler` — полный список задач, выбор и действия
  run / pause / resume / log; после каждого обновления маршрут
  перерегистрируется, поэтому данные свежие;
- слот `sidebar_content` — снимок списка на момент регистрации: V1 API не
  возвращает функцию отписки от слота, поэтому перерисовать его нельзя;
- команды палитры — действия, открытие панели, refresh, переход по списку
  (`Ctrl+Shift+J`, `Ctrl+Shift+↑/↓`, `Ctrl+Shift+Enter`);
- выбранная задача хранится в `api.kv` (`opencode-windows-scheduler.selected`);
- таймер 5 секунд и отписки снимаются в `api.lifecycle.onDispose`.

Ограничение слота — не регрессия, а свойство V1 API; в V2 панель обновляется
через reactive store `ctx.storage`.

**Хуки не используются осознанно.** Плагин не подписывается ни на
`ctx.tool.hook`, `ctx.permission.hook` и `ctx.event.subscribe` в V2, ни на
`Hooks.tool.execute.before/after`, `Hooks.event`, `Hooks.permission.ask` в V1:

- аудит — обёртка `withAudit` вокруг каждого инструмента в `createToolSpecs`,
  поэтому правила журнала одинаковы в обеих линиях и не зависят от hook-API;
- permissions — `resolvePermissions`/`buildOpencodeConfig` из
  `src/core/permissions.ts` в env фонового запуска, а не перехват вызовов;
- события — инструмент `emit_event`, file-watcher и git-trigger, поднятые в
  `createRuntime`.

Следствие для Д3: V1-адаптеру не нужны хуки — достаточно общих handlers и
`createRuntime`. `test-docs` следит, чтобы общий код не начал ссылаться на
V2-only домены без обновления этого раздела.

**Единая выгрузка.** Обе линии используют один `createShutdownHandler(runtime,
registrations)`: `shutdownGate.begin()` → освобождение регистраций →
`runtime.dispose()` → закрытие dashboard → ожидание активных in-process
операций → `closeDb()`. V2 отдаёт этот cleanup из `setup(ctx)`, V1 — из
`server()` (З3.1); порядок и таймаут `15_000` мс общие.

**Двойной экспорт.** В `src/index.ts`:

- `const v2Plugin = Plugin.define({ id, setup })` — entrypoint V2;
- `const v1Plugin: V1PluginModule = { id, server }` — entrypoint V1, `server()`
  вызывает `createV1Hooks()`;
- `export default { ...v2Plugin, ...v1Plugin }` — каждая линия читает свои поля
  (`setup` или `server`) и игнорирует чужие.

`createV1Hooks()` поднимает то же ядро (`createRuntime`), собирает те же
`createToolSpecs`, навешивает тот же `withAudit`, конвертирует `Tool.Result` в
V1 `ToolResult` (`{ output, metadata }`) и возвращает `Hooks` с `tool` и
`dispose`. Дашборд общий — `startSchedulerDashboard()`; GUI, RPC и скиллы в V1
не регистрируются, потому что их API там нет.

**Инструменты в V1.** `createV1Tools(runtime)` отдаёт все 26 спецификаций.
`args` — это `z.ZodRawShape` (`z.object(...).shape`), как требует V1 `tool()`;
схемы собраны корневым `zod@4.6.7`, а валидирует их копия `zod@4.1.8` из V1
SDK — совместимость мажора проверяется в `test-dual-entry.mjs`. У V1 `tool()`
нет параметра `options`, поэтому `codemode: true` в V1 не передаётся:
инструменты вызываются обычным способом, а не через code mode. На поведение это
не влияет — обработчики, аудит и результаты общие; отличие только в способе
вызова агентом.

## Как проверяется совместимость

| Проверка | Что покрывает |
|---|---|
| `test-dual-entry.mjs` | форму default export (`id`, `setup`, `server`), `createV1Hooks` → `tool` + `dispose`, 30 инструментов, совпадение имён с V2-реестром `createToolHandlers`, кросс-версию zod |
| `test-v1-integration.mjs` | реальный V1-путь: `server({ directory })`, изолированные `OPENCODE_SCHEDULER_HOME` и порт дашборда, три read-only инструмента, повторный `dispose` |
| `test-docs.mjs` | контракт в документации и коде: `exports["./tui"]`, `sidebar_content`, ключи `plugin`/`plugins`, инварианты состояния |
| CI `compat-v1` / `compat-v2` | отдельные jobs: V1 SDK `1.19.x` и V2 SDK `2.3.0` (устанавливается поверх `2.2.7`), не блокируют матрицу трёх ОС |

Полная загрузка через OpenCode CLI требует модели и рабочих кредов, поэтому в
CI она не запускается: `run` с боевыми ключами остаётся ручной проверкой.
Автоматически доказывается уровень entrypoint и реального `server()`, включая
SQLite, recovery и регистрацию инструментов.

## Где зафиксированы версии

| Что | Где | Значение |
|---|---|---|
| V2, сборка и runtime | `dependencies["@opencode/plugin"]` | `^2.2.7` |
| V2, схемы инструментов | `dependencies["@opencode/schema"]` | `^2.2.7` |
| V1, типы адаптера | `devDependencies["@opencode-ai/plugin"]` | `1.19.5` (pinned) |

`peerDependencies` намеренно не объявляются: plugin API — не runtime-зависимость
пакета, его предоставляет сам OpenCode. Пин V1 в `devDependencies` нужен, чтобы
адаптер компилировался против типов реальной V1-версии, а не «примерно похожей».
Изменение любого из этих трёх значений без правки таблицы роняет `test-docs`.

## Почему минимум V1 — 1.18.29

Двойная совместимость в одном пакете включается объектом
`{ ...Plugin.define({ id, setup }), async server() {...} }`: V2 вызывает
`setup()`, V1 вызывает `server()`. Этот способ появился в OpenCode `1.18.29`.
До него V1 умел только `server()`, а V2 — только `setup()`, поэтому один
default export не мог обслуживать обе линии. Для версий ниже нужен отдельный
legacy-entrypoint; в `1.5.6` его нет.

Проверено по реестру npm: версия `1.18.29` опубликована, последняя V1 — `1.19.5`.

## Почему минимум V2 — 2.2.7

Проверено по опубликованным типам `@opencode/plugin` (47 версий линии `2.x`):

| API | Появилось | Комментарий |
|---|---|---|
| `Plugin.define({ id, setup })` | `2.0.0` | ядро плагина |
| `ctx.tool.transform(editor => ...)` | `2.0.0` | регистрация инструментов |
| домены `ctx.*` (`location`, `storage`, `event`, `tool`, `session`, `permission`, `agent`, `shell`, `skill`, `command`, `mcp`, `worktree`, `rpc`) | `2.0.0` | набор одинаков с `2.2.7` |
| subpath `./gui` | `2.2.0` | в `2.1.4` ещё отсутствует (`404`) |
| subpath `./tui`, `./rpc` (через `./*`) | `2.0.0` | |

Минимум выставлен по **2.2.7**, а не по `2.0.0`, сознательно:

1. GUI — часть поверхности пакета (`exports` содержит `./gui-experimental`), а
   subpath `/gui` появился только в `2.2.0`.
2. Пакет собирается против типов `2.2.7` и объявляет зависимость `^2.2.7`.
   Версии ниже не проверяются, а значит не поддерживаются — обещать их нельзя.
3. Между `2.2.7` и `2.3.0` контракт `Plugin.define` и `ctx.tool.transform` не
   менялся, поэтому `2.3.0` проходит как проверочная версия.

Ядро (инструменты, хуки, SQLite, планировщик) технически работает и на `2.0.0`,
но GUI-часть там не загрузится. Поддержка `2.0.0–2.1.x` — отдельное решение,
в `1.5.6` его нет.

## Контракт V1

Всё ниже — из `@opencode-ai/plugin@1.19.5` (последняя V1-версия SDK).

**Экспорты пакета:** `.`, `./tool`, `./tui`, `./v2/*`. Subpath `/gui` и `/rpc`
отсутствуют — GUI-панель и RPC-методы в V1 недоступны.

**Тип модуля:**

```ts
type PluginInput = {
  client; project; directory; worktree; serverUrl; $
  experimental_workspace: { register(type, adapter): void }
}
type Plugin = (input: PluginInput, options?: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<Hooks>
type PluginModule = { id?: string; server: Plugin; tui?: never }
```

**Хуки (`Hooks`):** `dispose`, `event`, `config`, `tool` (карта инструментов),
`tool.execute.before`, `tool.execute.after`, `permission.ask`, `chat.message`,
`chat.params`, `chat.headers`, `command.execute.before`, `shell.env`, `auth`,
`provider`, а также группа `experimental.*`.

**Инструменты:** `tool({ description, args, execute })`, где `args` — raw shape
Zod-объекта. `@opencode-ai/plugin@1.19.5` зависит от `zod@4.1.8`, а пакет — от
`zod@^4.6.7`: мажор совпадает, отдельная копия zod для V1 не нужна. `execute`
получает `(args, context)` и возвращает `string` либо `{ title, output, metadata, attachments }`.

**TUI:** отдельный subpath `@opencode-ai/plugin/tui`; модуль TUI регистрируется
не через `setup(ctx)`, а через TUI-API V1 (`api.slots`, `api.route`, `api.kv`,
`api.command`). В `1.5.6` это `src/tui-v1.tsx`, который отдаётся из того же
`exports["./tui"]`, что и V2-модуль.

## Чего в V1 нет

| Возможность | Причина |
|---|---|
| GUI-панель | нет subpath `@opencode-ai/plugin/gui` |
| RPC-методы | нет subpath `@opencode-ai/plugin/rpc` |
| `ctx.storage` | контекст V1 не предоставляет storage; состояние — SQLite пакета |
